title: A theoretical study of subcarrier-wave quantum key distribution system integration with an optical transport network utilizing dense wavelength division multiplexing
authors: Fedor Kiselev, Natalia Veselkova, Roman Goncharov, Vladimir Egorov
abstract: In this paper we study the performance of subcarrier-wave quantum key distribution (SCW QKD) in the presence of classical channels of optical transport network utilizing dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM). We consider the impact of spontaneous Raman scattering noise as well as the four-wave mixing and channel isolation efficiency. We calculate quantum bit error rate as well as the secure key generation rate of SCW-QKD protocol for different parameters of DWDM system and quantum channel allocations. Our calculations show, that quantum channel allocation at the wavelength of 1310 nm is preferable to allocation at C-band due to lower nonlinear noise, despite fiber's larger attenuation at this wavelength.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes how noise from classical DWDM channels degrades Subcarrier-Wave Quantum Key Distribution (SCW QKD) systems. By calculating QBER and key rates, the authors demonstrate that placing the quantum channel at 1310 nm (O-band) significantly outperforms the C-band, primarily due to reduced nonlinear noise, which is crucial for practical network deployment.
main_problem: The paper investigates the performance limitations of Subcarrier-Wave Quantum Key Distribution (SCW QKD) when integrated into a classical optical transport network utilizing Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM).
main_result: Quantum channel allocation at the 1310 nm wavelength (O-band) is superior to the C-band because it mitigates nonlinear noise effects, leading to better achievable distances despite higher fiber attenuation.
method: The study involves theoretical calculations of the Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) and the secure key generation rate by modeling various noise sources.
model_or_system: The system models SCW QKD operating over an optical fiber shared with multiple classical DWDM channels. Noise sources analyzed include Spontaneous Raman Scattering (SpRS), Four-Wave Mixing (FWM), and Linear Channel Crosstalk (LCXT).
key_observables: Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER), secure key generation rate, and various noise power levels ($P_{ram}, P_{ijk}$).
important_parameters: Fiber length (L), attenuation ($\xi$), number of classical channels ($N_{ch}$), and the quantum channel allocation wavelength (1310 nm vs. C-band).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the use of output power for noise calculations and models the impact of noise sources on the overall detector click probability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of noise sources (SpRS, FWM) and the secure key generation rate on fiber length and the number of classical channels for both O-band and C-band configurations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the impact of classical DWDM noise on SCW QKD, deriving expressions for noise powers, calculating QBER and key rates, and comparing performance metrics across different wavelength allocations (O-band vs. C-band).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and quantum networks, as it provides quantitative guidelines for integrating quantum communication protocols into existing, high-capacity classical infrastructure.
